data.why: The app is fully self-contained: it loads its bundled models/celestial_model.pkl and data/sample.csv directly from the repo, with no file-upload widget, so nothing needs to be staged for the browser.

goals: Classify a celestial object as Galaxy, Star, or Quasar from its photometric magnitudes and redshift
Explore how changing individual photometric bands (u, g, r, i, z) shifts the predicted class and confidence
Sample a random real SDSS observation and see how the trained Random Forest classifies it
Inspect an object's spectral energy distribution across the five SDSS filters
Compare an object's position on color-color diagrams against the reference distributions of stars, galaxies, and quasars
Judge the reliability of a classification via the model's per-class confidence scores

review.summary: The tree captures what AstroClassify is for: classify one SDSS source from ugriz magnitudes and redshift, then check the call on the SED and color-color diagrams. The phases are sensible, the evidence is accurate, and the run honestly records that only the top-class confidence exists. It needs small fixes before filing: one wrong SED label, the missing step of testing the model against held-out records (whose true class the UI never shows), and a looser cut of the Plotly-controls feature.
